questions.q: Why can training on recorded sales give a model that under-forecasts?
options: Sales data has too many rows
Sales are capped by available stock, so demand on stock-out days is hidden
why: Row count is not the problem.
Noise alone does not create a bias.
Models can use sales; the issue is what they mean.

questions.q: Put the design steps in a good order.
questions.why: Start with the decision, then data, model, evaluation, serving, and monitoring.

questions.q: A grocery chain has 1 500 stores and 20 000 SKUs. About 30% of the store-SKU pairs are active. How many series is that?
Scenario: in food delivery, your model predicts low demand for a zone at 19:00, the app sends fewer couriers, and delivery times rise. What is this risk called?
options: A feedback loop between the forecast and the system
why: Drift may also occur, but the main issue is that your decision changes the data.
Correct: the forecast influences supply, which influences orders.
Cold start is about new items.
Overfitting is about training data fit.

questions.q: Scenario: an interviewer asks for the evaluation. Which plan is best?
options: Rolling-origin backtest over several recent periods, WAPE and bias vs seasonal naive, by segment
why: Random splits leak the future and MAPE breaks on small values.
Training error says little about the future.

questions.q: Which features are usually known in advance and useful for retail demand? (pick all)
why: That is the target. It is leakage.
